name: Abd al-Qahir al-Tabrizi
bio: Jamal al-Din Abd al-Qahir ibn Muhammad al-Tabrizi was a Shafi'i judge, preacher and poet. His family came from Bukhara; he was born in Harran in 648 AH (1250 CE), brought to Damascus at six, and grew up and studied there. He told his student al-Dhahabi that as a boy his uncle strangled him, threw him into a pit and covered him with earth and stones, where he lay for days until a passer-by pulled him out, and that the uncle took his inheritance to Yemen. He was a judge in Salamiyya, Ajlun and Safad until the judge al-Qazwini dismissed him, al-Dhahabi says, “because he did not explain away but affirmed”; he then moved to Egypt and was judge of Damietta until he died there in 740 AH (1339 CE), aged 92. He collected his sermons in a volume called Tuhfat al-Alibba', and al-Safadi wrote that his verse was “sweet and flowing”.
